title: Nos Vemos en las Urnas · Lean development plan
subtitle: Free comparison and private quiz · owner-supplied sources · minimal infrastructure
summary: Build a useful public service: cite and compare supplied electoral programmes, run a short progressive quiz locally, explain policy overlaps only after explicit finish, and collect narrowly scoped voluntary privacy-protected aggregate feedback. Remove the editorial backoffice and mandatory human-review/language machinery.
status: Authorized scaffold restart; local implementation in progress; no public launch approval.
baseline: Spanish public UI; English original code/docs
30 commit steps; 28 core and two optional
One PHP app, static bundles and SQLite counters; no runtime ML

sections.title: 1. Product and deliberate cuts
sections.lead: A free public service with two primary entry points: compare programmes or take the quiz.
items: The owner supplies electoral documents. Visitors can explore public sources without taking the quiz, or answer a short quiz and explicitly request results. Both journeys share the same versioned evidence.

Keep citations, inclusion, privacy, honest scoring, accessibility and working CI. Remove editorial accounts, MFA/invitations, reviewer identities/qualifications, approval quorums, adjudication, review queues and staff audit workflows.

No recruited panels, mandatory external fluent/legal/security reviewer roster, human calibration studies, multi-operator cryptography project or regional-language launch programme. Automated checks do not become claims of perfect correctness.
No runtime model service, Rubix ML, voter classifier, recommendation optimizer, electoral forecasts, voter registration/account, party-specific analytics, demographics or intended-vote collection.
Cut the old 180-step sequence to 30 coherent commits, with 28 core steps and two optional extensions. The authorized scaffold restart preserves existing work in the verified private external backup.

sections.title: 2. Public journeys
sections.lead: The comparison tool and quiz must each be useful on their own.
items: Home: two clear actions, what the service measures, how sources work, privacy in one plain paragraph, and the source release date.

Comparison: browse all in-scope candidacies, select two or more, search topics and see exact proposals, differences, overlap and evidence gaps. Provide a table on wide screens and readable cards on phones.

Quiz: explain local processing and reload behavior, optional local constituency selection, balanced questions, skip/unsure, optional topic priorities and edit. After ten presented questions offer finish, five more, review or exit. Presentation count and scored-answer count differ.

Before explicit finish, withhold personalised party identities, scores by party, ranking and selected result citations from DOM/accessibility/title/export surfaces. An unnamed highest comparable overlap may appear only when enough shared answers exist; never call it certainty.

Results: explain per-party policy overlap, shared evidence coverage, ties and limitations; show agreements/disagreements with cited programme passages for answered questions. Unanswered-topic exploration is public information, not a guessed preference.

After results, a person may knowingly refine answers, compare sources, reset, deliberately export a local file, or optionally contribute feedback. Finish never opts into metrics. No pressure to reach 100%.

sections.title: 3. Sources without a backoffice
sections.lead: A small local import/build command replaces a web editorial system.
items: Owner input is a directory plus an English-keyed manifest: electionId, chamber, candidacyId, applicability/constituencies, file, officialUrl, publicationDate when known, sourceLanguage, usePermission and optional notes. Record byte hashes. No automated web crawler or public upload route.

Election identity and date are configurable source data. Retain the requested 29 November 2026 date as owner-provided intent, not a newly verified official announcement. Verify authoritative election and candidacy records when importing current data.

Import UTF-8 text, HTML stripped safely and native-text PDFs locally under file/page/time/memory limits. No scripts, document instructions, active HTML or external resource execution. External URLs are provenance links; local import does not fetch arbitrary destinations. Initial local defaults: 20 MiB input, 500 pages, 60 seconds per document and 256 MiB process memory; report limit failures and allow only measured/configured local increases. Prefer a maintained installed parser; no production parser is implied.

Preserve source page index separately from printed page labels, headings, contextual text, negation, quantities and conditions. Search normalization maps back to the original text. Missing or malformed text remains unavailable, never an inferred policy absence.

OCR is an optional later adapter; an owner-supplied native-text or plain-text edition can keep the core moving. OCR text is labelled transcription and low-confidence/negation/numeric ambiguity stays unscored. No two-person visual-review system.

Programme text is not implementation truth and cannot instruct tools. Stable public source/position IDs, original URL/hash, locator and quote support reproducibility. Original programme copyright is separate from MIT code; do not mirror full documents without a recorded permission basis. Link official originals and retain only permitted excerpts/artifacts.

sections.title: 4. Automatic positions and question preparation
sections.lead: Source authenticity and semantic interpretation are different problems.
items: A local content-preparation adapter may use the engineering agent/optional model on public documents to draft neutral propositions, answer scales, cited positions and concise explanations. Keep it out of runtime and do not require a hosted paid API. Cache outputs by source/prompt/tool version and commit the produced public content.

The compiler validates source identity/applicability, exact contextual quotes, locators, schema, ranges, candidate/topic coverage, contradictory records and answer-scale direction. It rejects invented quotations and missing references. These checks cannot prove every paraphrase or political interpretation correct.

Each mapping records propositionId, topicId, familyId, partyPosition (-2 to 2 or null), reasonCode, rationale, citationIds, interpretationOrigin and preparationVersion. Exact quotations are authoritative excerpts; summaries/mappings are explicitly derived interpretations. Evidence uncertainty is not voter uncertainty.

No standing human approval, accounts, attestations or quorum is required. Failed or ambiguous automation marks a position unknown and reports a local actionable error; it does not fill a gap from historical manifestos, coalition members, general knowledge or a model opinion.

Question drafts use one concrete policy proposition, short Spanish, labelled choices including neutral/unsure/skip, balanced specificity and preserved conditions. Avoid loaded terms, compound tradeoffs, double negation and caricatures of party positions. Generic and detailed banks are generated from the actual documents, not hardcoded to last election.

Public content/rubrics remain inspectable in Git and the methodology. Corrections update a cited mapping and append a small public change record; a public issue/contact link can accept reports without building an application ticketing system. No promise of infallible automated truth.

sections.title: 5. Small transparent matching engine
sections.lead: The runtime is deterministic arithmetic, with no ML.
items: Use numeric agreement scale -2,-1,0,1,2. Unsure/skip have no numeric value. For answer a and cited position p, similarity = 1 - abs(a-p)/4. Party overlap = 100 * sum(w * similarity)/sum(w) for the disclosed scored set. Scores are independent and do not sum to 100.

Weights are release-defined topic and question-family budgets, with optional explicit user topic priorities (0,1,2) kept locally. Divide each family budget across its declared question items; do not let a long topic or repeated variants gain accidental weight. Freeze the bank and weight definition for a session.

For a ranking or highest-overlap checkpoint, use the same answered propositions and weights for every candidacy in the disclosed comparison cohort. The default cohort includes all applicable supplied candidacies. A deliberately selected narrower cohort is prominently labelled; other candidacies remain visible.

Initial conservative display threshold: eight numeric answers, four topics, and at least 60% of answered positive weight shared across the cohort. Missing sources stay visible. If the threshold fails, show cited comparisons and separately labelled partial overlaps/coverage without ordering or declaring a winner. These are engineering heuristics, not statistically calibrated confidence.

Display overlap, response/evidence coverage and question count separately. A 60% overlap says that the observed weighted answers align by that index; it does not mean 60% probability that the person prefers that party. More answers can lower the index.

Keep the existing v1 reference as a historical arithmetic oracle. Implement the final browser engine against the simpler explicit weight contract and pin its version. Test exact examples, unknown/zero weights, ties, common-denominator fairness, permutation invariance and locale invariance. No elaborate completion bounds or robust-leader certification is required.

sections.title: 6. Progressive question order
sections.lead: Start useful and get more specific without pretending to read minds.
items: Start with ten general questions covering the released topics, one per family where possible, selected by a documented balanced order. Do not force scoring if enough comparable evidence does not exist.

For continuation, prioritize uncovered positive-weight topics/families first, then specificity. Among eligible remaining questions, compute D(q)=(max party position-min party position)/4 on the close-profile common-evidence cohort, U(t)=1-answered numeric bank weight in topic t/total positive released topic weight, and score(q)=topicPriority*(0.6*U(t)+0.4*D(q))/burden(q). Default burdens: general=1, specific=1.5; all values/version are published. Unsupported numeric spread is zero. Stable question ID breaks equal scores.

Define close profiles as within ten observed index points of the current highest comparable index. If comparison is insufficient, consider the full cohort. Never remove parties from results or infer an answer; stable question IDs and party renaming/order do not change semantic selection.

Limit a family to two presented questions per session by default; score its declared items using the fixed family budget, without double-counting alternate wording of the same proposition. An edit resets derived selection; already presented questions remain in local history. Identical profiles or no discrimination are legitimate outcomes.

If the selector fails or exceeds its CPU budget, use the balanced remaining order with the same scoring contract. Bank exhaustion offers explicit finish/exit; it never reveals automatically. There is no prediction probability or target of reaching 100%.

sections.title: 7. Private quiz boundary
sections.lead: The server distributes public content; it does not receive a visitor profile.
items: Serve the same complete public election bank for everyone. Filter constituency/candidacies, calculate scores and choose questions in the browser. Do not fetch party/question-specific data in response to answers or private selection.

No quiz session API, cookies, localStorage, default IndexedDB, answer persistence, URL/hash encoding, telemetry, replay, advertising scripts, crash payloads or support dumps containing answers, priorities, scope, scores or next-question IDs.

A local download is deliberate, clearly explains its political contents and stays on the device. Restart clears memory. Shared links may reference only public sources/topics with no personal selections or result.

Network operators still process connection metadata; privacy copy says so. Configure app, reverse proxy, host error reporting and backups consistently. No claim that local matching makes all HTTP traffic anonymous.
Metrics are a separate voluntary flow described below. They never reuse or upload the full quiz vector and never include party affinity or voting intention.

sections.title: 8. Agreement metrics with a bounded privacy design
sections.lead: Measure voluntary contributions, not voters or the electorate.
items: Two purposes: (1) whether the result broadly fits the person (yes/no/unsure, with no party/score), and (2) agreement/neutral/disagreement with one randomly sampled public policy proposition. Present the latter as a separate short survey, independently of answered quiz topics, with optional refusal.

The proposition is sampled uniformly from a small fixed public survey bank, independently of the profile. Select one proposition per opt-in visit and never automatically copy a quiz answer. Record its question/wording version. Topic labels aggregate fixed propositions and cannot be treated as universal agreement with a broad topic.

Before sending, apply documented three-category randomized response using crypto.getRandomValues and epsilon=1: report the real category with probability exp(1)/(exp(1)+2), otherwise uniformly one of the other two. Thus raw agreement and result-fit values never leave the device. A maximum of two reports per visit gives epsilon=2 composition for that visit; repeat visits are not a lifetime bound.

One stateless POST endpoint accepts only metricId, public surveyVersion/propositionId as applicable, protocolVersion and one randomized category. Never send answers, score, party, constituency, demographics, persistent IDs, precise client time or a shared report/session identifier. Schema rejects extra fields and oversized bodies. Submission is best-effort: one attempt per chosen metric per visit, with no automatic retry or durable retry queue. A failed/lost acknowledgement is skipped; do not inflate counts or compose unrecorded privacy budget through repeated independent randomization.

Increment SQLite counters atomically by server-selected week, survey version, metric/proposition and reported category. Do not retain individual event rows or request bodies. Disable body/IP/access telemetry for this route throughout the stack; ordinary transient connection metadata is still present. Keep only counters for the election and a bounded retention period.

Estimate each category fraction from reported fraction r: estimate=(r-1/(exp(1)+2))/((exp(1)-1)/(exp(1)+2)). Build multinomial-compatible uncertainty from reported counts; do not disguise clipping, sampling noise or impossible noisy estimates. Suppress public values below 500 contributions or above ten percentage points of interval half-width. Topic summaries use equal proposition weight only when all included propositions have adequate coverage; disclose that set. For display, use the three-category constrained multinomial maximum-likelihood estimate on the simplex, retain the unbounded inverse estimate in methodology/report diagnostics, and transform simultaneous Wilson intervals on the reported categories (95% family confidence, Bonferroni z≈2.394) through the same affine inverse. Label constraints/noise; do not present clipped values as certainty. A reported interval wholly outside the protocol-feasible probability range flags unreliable data and suppresses that snapshot. The sampling model assumes independent honest randomized contributions, which the public endpoint cannot guarantee.

Publish closed weekly static reports, with sample size, uncertainty, survey wording and method. No party/vote charts, demographic/constituency cuts, real-time counter API or arbitrary filters. Result-fit counters have no party dimension. Do not sort topics whose uncertainty overlaps into a confident league table.

Without identities, unique people and strict one-person-one-vote cannot be established. Counters describe opt-in contributions and can be biased/abused. Use bounded payloads, concurrency/global request budgets and automatic collection pause on anomalies; avoid accounts, fingerprinting or retained IP hashes as a workaround.

Randomization and aggregation reduce disclosure; they do not alone prove legal anonymity or remove political-opinion rules. Treat this as privacy-protected aggregate feedback, with truthful notice and clear opt-in. Validate the actual host/proxy/log flow and applicable Spanish legal basis before enabling collection; no mandatory consultant/staff review workflow is introduced. If that flow cannot meet the documented boundary, disable this endpoint while the free quiz/comparison remain available.

Prepare and test this small branch before documents arrive. Live collection and any public statistical report require the launch action to explicitly include their flags/actual flow; do not activate them from a passing synthetic test.

sections.title: 9. Language and inclusive interface
sections.lead: Spanish is the complete initial UI; translations are optional content work.
items: Original code, file/route/schema/API/translation keys, reason codes, comments, tests and developer docs are English. Product copy, errors, accessibility labels, privacy/help, insights and exports are Spanish. Use existing lang/es catalogs and APP_LOCALE/APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE=es.

Reuse the existing small dictionary/key/placeholder checks; do not build more translation bureaucracy or spend cycles translating unused admin screens. No admin surface is in scope. Missing keys must have a safe Spanish fallback rather than an exception string.

Catalan, Basque and Galician are optional later packs, not a core dependency. Use the same IDs/scales/rubrics, complete the enabled public surface and test meaning/score parity. AI can draft translations; no mandated human certification or reviewer service. If a translation is uncertain, keep that pack disabled and disclose its status.

Original official quotations/proper names remain exact, including their original language. Any translated paraphrase is separately labelled and the original remains reachable. Do not score a different meaning across locales.

Use the modern UI foundations already prepared where useful: clear hierarchy, readable text, restrained motion, fast feedback, mobile comparison cards, no party-dominant visual bias. Native controls, visible focus, keyboard flow, screen-reader labels, contrast, reduced motion, zoom/reflow and generous targets are acceptance checks.

Automated browser/axe checks plus a short reproducible keyboard/mobile checklist are enough for this project workflow; no recruited mixed-age research programme or named assistive-device panel is a launch prerequisite. Do not claim universal accessibility certification from automated tests.

sections.title: 10. Minimal infrastructure and free access
sections.lead: Start with one small PHP host; Node and source processing run at build time.
items: Laravel/Blade/Tailwind plus focused TypeScript, existing Boost/skills for development only. Serve immutable compressed JSON and local assets from the same host. No runtime Node process, Redis, PostgreSQL, persistent extraction worker, queue cluster, Elasticsearch, third-party analytics, external font dependency or hosted model.

Use SQLite only for aggregate counters/operational data that genuinely need storage, with transactions, WAL/busy-timeout where supported and concurrency tests. Source content lives in versioned files; do not recreate the editorial database as a content CMS. If counters become a bottleneck, batch/report less first and add infrastructure only after measurement.

Build/import on the owner/developer machine or a bounded CI job, then deploy the generated data/assets. Production contains the web runtime, immutable bundles and counter DB; no OCR tooling, Boost/MCP, source-upload endpoint or development fixtures.

Initial working budget: one supported PHP host with roughly 1 vCPU/1 GiB RAM and persistent disk. This is a starting target to measure, not a throughput guarantee or a provider price. TLS, compressed caching, daily encrypted off-host backup of counters/config and immutable release files, and one restore command are sufficient.

Free means no charge to visitors. Hosting/domain/backups still have owner costs; choose the existing/cheapest adequate host using a current quote before any purchase. The preferred .es domain remains unverified/unpurchased. No provider, cloud product, Valet or paid analytics is mandated.

Proposed budgets: initial compressed assets <=300 KiB, complete evidence/quiz bank <=5 MiB compressed, local selection/scoring <=100 ms p95 on a declared mid-range/mobile test profile. Loading readiness has a separate measured target. Respect actual cold-load timings; optimize measured bottlenecks rather than building a distributed platform.

sections.title: 11. Checks, publication and operation
sections.lead: Keep checks that protect a real public service; remove staff and certification machinery.
items: Every implementation commit still passes python3 scripts/check-staged.py on its exact staged tree, including required local CI and preserved security hooks. No --no-verify or failed/skipped/unavailable checks. Hosted checks for the actual pushed revision remain separate; no automatic push is authorized.

Meaningful regression coverage: import/citation corruption and parser limits; unsupported/conflicting evidence; exact score examples and common-denominator invariants; browser-local requests/storage; explicit result reveal; source links; mobile/keyboard/axe; metric payload/noise/counter races/refusal/failure; schema/hash/update/withdrawal; backup/restore.

One actual public-launch approval remains for concrete external action/costs/domain/release and any metric/statistic activation included in it. Prepare that packet only after the implementation and applicable tests are reviewable. No separate blueprint, methodology, human quorum, language panel or backoffice gates.

Owner source provision is an input, not a staff approval process. Local source-independent engineering can continue before current documents arrive. Build complete synthetic journeys first; current publication needs actual compatible documents and candidacy metadata.

Pin sessions to a bundle. Routine releases do not change answers silently; a fixed public withdrawal check can invalidate a compromised release and offer restart. Atomic switch and one-command rollback retain a change history. Degrade to comparison/quoted evidence when scoring is unavailable; metric failures never block either core journey.

Prepare a simple release checklist/runbook: configured domain/TLS, original-source permissions, non-dev production assets, actual traffic/log/storage probe, basic load, counter backup/restore, previous-bundle rollback and one owner/contact route. No on-call roster, staff capacity matrix or enterprise RPO contract.

Keep supplied plans and historical/synthetic fixtures labelled by election/purpose. Future election updates replace content/bank mappings through the same tools, not a new editorial application. Future maintenance is ongoing operation, not a task an agent can certify forever complete.

sections.title: 12. Reuse prepared work and retire the old scope
sections.lead: The owner explicitly authorized a one-time unpublished local restart after a verified complete external backup.
items: The original scaffold commit remains unchanged; unpublished implementation commits and prepared files are preserved in the private external backup.
Retain useful CI fixes, canonical skills and the standalone cleanup intent. Remove superseded auth/backoffice, approval machinery and historical planning from the active tree.
Do not rewrite remote history, push, change identity/signing, delete backups or real documents, deploy, purchase or activate collection.
Implement and verify eligible lean tasks; actual current sources and hosted launch evidence remain separate inputs.

requirements.title: Free consumer service
requirements.acceptance: No paywall, visitor account, backoffice, ads, partisan funding features or runtime AI dependency.

requirements.title: Owner-supplied current sources
requirements.acceptance: The owner supplies the source files and provenance manifest. Election/chamber/applicability and missing candidacies are explicit. Historical samples never become current evidence.

requirements.title: Exact citations and honest interpretation
requirements.acceptance: Every displayed source claim and scored position has a contextual locator. Automated interpretations are identified as interpretations; ambiguous, conflicting or unsupported positions are unknown.

requirements.title: Useful public comparison
requirements.acceptance: Browse programmes, search topics, select candidacies locally, compare promises with citations and visible coverage. No question answering is required.

requirements.title: Private deterministic matching
requirements.acceptance: Answers, priorities, constituency, scores and adaptive state stay in browser memory by default. Independent policy overlaps are not vote predictions or confidence probabilities.

requirements.title: Short progressive quiz
requirements.acceptance: Ten balanced starter questions, optional five-question blocks, skip/unsure and edit. Reveal party results only on explicit finish. More answers can raise or lower overlap.

requirements.title: Fair evidence and question weights
requirements.acceptance: Do not rank different evidence sets. Preserve candidacies, unknowns and ties. Fixed topic/family budgets limit redundant questions and leading wording.

requirements.title: Clear Spanish and inclusive design
requirements.acceptance: Spanish v1, English original code/docs, responsive accessible fast UI. Optional regional translations preserve meaning and scoring; no reviewer workforce or language-certification gates.

requirements.title: Relevant voluntary aggregate feedback
requirements.acceptance: Include result-fit feedback and agreement with policy propositions. Separate opt-in, randomized limited contributions, counters only, uncertainty and honest sample/anonymity limits.

requirements.title: Cheap operational footprint
requirements.acceptance: One Laravel deployment with static bundles and SQLite counters. Build/import locally. No mandatory Redis, PostgreSQL, queue worker, object-store split, ML service or analytics provider.

requirements.title: Reproducible updates and recovery
requirements.acceptance: Validate schema/hashes, pin sessions, atomically switch bundles, support correction/withdrawal and restore the previous release plus counters.

requirements.title: Meaningful checks and disciplined commits
requirements.acceptance: Retain all required exact-staged CI checks and security hooks; no bypass. Work directly on main, preserve existing work, record actual checks and keep production claims separate.

releaseContract.capabilityIsolation: Metrics and optional translations never block independently passing comparison/quiz.

policy.evidence: Actual commands/artifact hashes; local engineering does not certify production; preserve historical reports.

approvalGates.requiredEvidence: Actual release checks, source provenance/permissions, authorized host flow/logs and restore/rollback; truthful metric notice/basis if enabled. No staff/quorum requirements.

Presentation count differs from answered weight; insufficient evidence gets plain text, not a fabricated number.
verification: Ten-plus-five, many skips, bank exhaustion, no common evidence, keyboard/reduced-motion checks.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: feat: reveal cited results after deliberate finish
deliverables: Party overlaps/ties, coverage and answered-topic agreement/disagreement with exact citations and refinement action.
acceptanceCriteria: Results use pinned release and same-set ordering rules; no voting intention/probability or inferred unanswered beliefs.
Explicit finish required even after exhaustion; refinement acknowledges already seen parties.
verification: Reveal/non-reveal, score-citation parity, partial/tie/unknown, withdrawal and informed-refinement flows.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: feat: polish the fast accessible public experience
deliverables: Coherent modern home/comparison/quiz/results; responsive controls, focus, text/contrast and restrained motion.
acceptanceCriteria: Spanish public/error/accessibility/help strings; no effort on unused admin languages.
Keyboard/axe/reflow/reduced-motion and declared asset/cold-load/local-CPU budgets pass; no invented participant certification.
verification: Public browser flows at mobile/desktop, axe, keyboard checklist and measured build/CPU/load budgets.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: test: verify local reset export and private quiz traffic
deliverables: Explicit local export, clear-file warning, complete reset and automated whole-journey privacy assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: Exports never reveal unfinished results or upload a profile.
No private state in requests/URLs/cookies/storage/errors; comparison and result/source navigation use public assets only.
verification: Intercept actual browser traffic/storage across answer/edit/finish/refine/export/exit/restart and failure flows.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: feat: add voluntary randomized feedback on fit and policies
deliverables: Separate opt-in result-fit and random public policy survey, fixed schema and epsilon=1 randomized response per metric.
acceptanceCriteria: Never reuse quiz answers or include party/scores/scope. Refusal/failure leaves core usable.
crypto RNG, category mapping and per-visit composition are explicit; repeat visits are not falsely bounded or unique voters.
verification: Deterministic injected-RNG branches, distribution/estimator fixtures, consent/no-consent and independent survey selection.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: feat: store bounded aggregate counters in SQLite
deliverables: Stateless strict-schema aggregate endpoint and atomic weekly categorical counters only.
acceptanceCriteria: Reject profile fields/free text/IDs/oversize/unknown versions; no raw event rows/body logging or Laravel session.
WAL/locking/busy timeout measured on intended SQLite setup; counter failure safely skips contributions.
verification: HTTP schema/no-cookie/error/body logging and parallel counter updates/retries/global budget tests.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: feat: report aggregate agreement with uncertainty
deliverables: CLI report estimator and closed-week static snapshots with survey wording, counts, uncertainty and suppression.
acceptanceCriteria: Minimum 500 contributions and <=10pp interval half-width; no demographic/party/geography/real-time filtering.
Equal-proposition topic summaries disclose coverage; statistical overlap/negative noise and voluntary/bot bias remain explicit.
verification: Known randomized counts, small cells, impossible estimates, intervals, incomplete topics and snapshot differencing boundaries.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: test: verify metric privacy refusal failures and limits
deliverables: End-to-end metric schema/log/storage inventory, anomaly pause and documented host-probe commands.
acceptanceCriteria: Raw local selections do not appear outside browser; payloads contain only approved randomized symbols/public IDs.
Default collection disabled until actual launch flow passes; no claim of guaranteed anonymity/unique people or election prediction.
verification: Opt-in/refusal/retries/outage/malicious payload/aggregate concurrency browser+HTTP tests; no production collection.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: data: import supplied current programmes and regenerate the bank
deliverables: Real owner-supplied current manifests/programmes, coverage and grounded compiled questions/positions.
acceptanceCriteria: No human-review workforce; automated compiler outputs are cited and labelled.
Actual dates/candidacies/election/permissions checked against supplied authoritative records; no silent historical fallback.
verification: Real-source import/compiler/citation checks and inspect generated coverage/error report; keep provenance.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: chore: prepare one-host deployment backup and rollback
deliverables: Portable Laravel/static/SQLite production template, local build/import workflow, encrypted backup and restore/rollback commands.
acceptanceCriteria: No paid provisioning or deployment in this commit; no Boost/dev/parser/worker in public runtime.
TLS/caching/log/DB permissions and backup retention documented for one host; existing source/counter data preserved.
Source-only/core deployment remains independently preparable. Include counter backup/concurrency checks when L022 exists; otherwise keep collection disabled and record the missing metric branch.
verification: Production-mode local smoke, SQLite backup during writes, restore/hash/previous-bundle and missing-disk checks.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: test: verify complete release candidate and recovery
deliverables: Coherent actual-source local release candidate and scoped test/load/privacy/citation/recovery report.
acceptanceCriteria: All applicable current-source/quiz/comparison/privacy/a11y/security/asset checks pass for the exact core candidate. Include metric checks only when L024 has passed and collection is proposed; otherwise explicitly keep collection disabled.
Synthetic passes do not substitute for actual hosted proxy/log/TLS evidence; remaining host facts are clearly listed.
verification: Full unchanged CI, representative full bank browser journeys, real source parity, bounded load and restore/rollback.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: docs: prepare the single concrete public launch action
deliverables: One launch packet with exact release/domain/provider/quote, public and metric flags, host probe results/remaining inputs and rollback.
acceptanceCriteria: No fabricated user approval and no publication/purchase/live collection within packet preparation.
One owner action approves only the named scope/costs; metrics may stay disabled without blocking quiz/comparison. No staffing gates.

A passing core packet does not require L021-L024 completion. Metric activation additionally requires L024 evidence and the actual hosted flow/notice; incomplete metrics are visibly disabled, never silently certified.
verification: Check packet hashes/config against candidate; hosted probes only on already authorized infrastructure.
If no host is authorized, mark actual flow pending and supply reproducible commands; do not claim launch-ready.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: feat: optionally import image-only programmes with local OCR
deliverables: Optional bounded local OCR/transcription adapter, model/tool versions and quality flags.
acceptanceCriteria: No production OCR service, staff visual attestations or forced scanned-source adoption.
Keep original page images/links where permitted; uncertain negation/numbers/conditions unscored. Label OCR rather than claiming source-exact parity.
verification: Real local OCR quality/limits on permitted samples and low-confidence/quantity/negation failures.
reuseCandidates: Prepared OCR machinery stripped of reviewer requirements only if simpler than replacement
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commits.subject: feat: optionally translate the public interface
deliverables: Optional complete ca/gl/eu public packs with original quotations preserved and identical semantic IDs.
acceptanceCriteria: No formal fluent reviewer/quorum gate; uncertainty is disclosed and incomplete/uncertain packs stay disabled.
No admin translations or impact on scores, weights, citations, consent and private state.
verification: Enabled key/placeholder and public-browser coverage, semantic/score/selection parity; keep existing checks.
commits.rollback: Revert the bounded change while preserving existing data and the previous public bundle.

commitPlan.progressPolicy: Each L ID is a bounded commit-sized deliverable. Do not mark completed from older C IDs without verifying its changed acceptance. Future maintenance is a reusable tool/runbook, not permanent completion.

owner_current_programmes_and_manifest.description: Owner-provided current documents, candidacy/election/applicability and provenance manifest; real files with hashes, not a reviewer signoff.

risks.title: Automated semantic error
risks.mitigation: Exact context, explicit interpretation labels, unknown/conflict handling and public corrections; no promise that source matching proves every interpretation.

risks.title: Insufficient comparable evidence
risks.mitigation: Keep candidacies and coverage; same-set scoring or cited partial comparison without broad ranking.

risks.title: Feedback disclosure or unreliable statistics
risks.mitigation: Separate sampled/noisy contributions, no profile/IDs/event log, bounded counters, uncertainty/suppression and actual hosted flow; no guarantee of anonymity or representative people.

risks.title: Overbuilt prepared code
risks.mitigation: Reconcile useful utilities and tests, remove unused runtime/admin machinery coherently; preserve history and existing non-synthetic data.

risks.title: Small-host contention or source availability
risks.mitigation: Static bundles/cache first, measure SQLite concurrency and payload budgets; comparison remains useful when quiz/metrics unavailable.

sources.label: AEPD: anonymous data definition
sources.note: Anonymous means a person is not identifiable; names/identifiers alone do not settle this.

sources.label: WP29 Opinion 05/2014 via AEPD
sources.note: Aggregation/noise techniques have limitations; assess singling-out, linkage and inference. Not a certification of the proposed protocol.
